INTEGRATED ARCHITECTURAL SYNTHESIS
“An airport is not only physical infrastructure. It is a continuously moving information network where safety and punctuality depend on every communication link.”

The 12 actors operate as interdependent nodes. When information flows smoothly across channels — from VHF radio to AODB datalinks — the airport maintains operational equilibrium. When a node disconnects or an exchange breaks down, cascading delays propagate across the entire aviation ecosystem.

01 · PHYSICAL ZONES
Landside forecourt, terminal concourses, baggage make-up basement, apron ramp, taxiways, and dual active runways (09R/27L).
02 · HUMAN & AGENCY ACTORS
12 distinct operational, security, and commercial groups with strict jurisdictional boundaries and high interdependency.
03 · TECHNICAL CHANNELS
Redundant transmission media spanning sub-millisecond VHF radio, dedicated crash bells, AODB/AOMS datalinks, and DCS CUPPS networks.
04 · SYNCHRONIZED DECISIONS
Collaborative Decision Making (A-CDM) aligning target takeoff times, pushback approvals, gate allocations, and passenger clearance.
